_readme: GENERATED by scripts/required-checks-generate.sh from check runs actually observed on the sampled shas. Never hand-edit a context string: GitHub validates neither the name nor the app_id, and a typo deadlocks the branch forever (honest-gates D21).

enforced=true means protection IS applied to this branch. From this commit an unreadable or absent protection config is a HARD failure in scripts/required-checks-verify.sh — it is no longer a committed pre-flip state. The reversal is one attributable command: `bash scripts/required-checks-apply.sh --disable --confirm`.

THE SAMPLING RULE, written down rather than tribal (hgw2-s7). The set below is the INTERSECTION over the sampled heads, so the sample decides what may be required. Sample at least TWO heads that are POST-SHIM and DISPATCHER-SUCCEEDED — `Dispatch (changed-path sets)` must be present and successful on each. A head where that name is ABSENT predates the always-running dispatcher, its job-level `if:` decisions were never made, and no re-run rescues it: re-running a workflow that did not exist at that sha produces nothing. Sample ONE head that EXERCISES the Elixir matrix (`Test (Elixir 1.18.1 / OTP 27.0)` rendered and concluded) and ONE that SKIPS it (the same job publishes the uninterpolated template name `Test (Elixir ${{ matrix.elixir }} / OTP ${{ matrix.otp }})`). Both shapes must still render the aggregators, and that is exactly what makes an aggregator — not a leaf job — the only safe thing to require. This file was generated from 08437ad (matrix exercised) and ecfd2890 (matrix skipped).

THE FLOOR IS A SEPARATE ARTIFACT, and regenerating this file without it is how the required set silently shrinks. `bash scripts/required-checks-floor.sh <candidate>` asserts the candidate is a SUPERSET of `git show origin/main:.github/required-checks.json` on context AND app_id. A bare count floor is not enough: a specimen that swaps `Elixir gate` for an advisory keeps the count at 2 and passes it (honest-gates D64, D74).

EXCLUSIONS ARE WHAT THE SAMPLE SAW, never a complete census. A workflow that never triggered on either sampled head renders no name at all, so it cannot appear below. Disqualification is a property of workflow TOPOLOGY, not of a workflow's identity: a workflow is structurally disqualified FOR AS LONG AS it carries a workflow-level `on: paths:` filter, because such a filter emits NO check run on a PR that misses the paths, and a required context that is ABSENT reports 'expected' forever (D18). `security.yml` is excluded on exactly that basis today — still paths-filtered to api/** — and independently because its mix-audit job is red on `main`. `console-harness.yml` (and `cloud.yml`) were excluded on the same topology grounds, and are being shimmed this round so an always-running aggregator job emits a check on every PR; once those shims land the topology objection no longer applies to them and their aggregator contexts become registrable. Two legacy Vercel commit statuses fail on EVERY sha repo-wide and live in a different namespace (R0/R3); they can never be required.

Every protection field is enumerated INCLUDING the falses: the PUT does not converge omitted state (allow_force_pushes resets, required_linear_history and required_conversation_resolution do NOT). See honest-gates D41.

No workflow carries a merge_group trigger and this repo is user-owned (no merge queue), so queue semantics are not a variable today. If the repo ever moves to an org and the merge queue is enabled, every required check would sit Pending-forever in the merge group on day one.

OPERATIONAL: a required context whose LATEST run on the head concluded `cancelled` blocks the merge with a third refusal shape (`... is cancelled.`, honest-gates D38) and clears only on a re-run or a push. elixir.yml sets cancel-in-progress on PR refs, so a superseded head can leave one behind. That is a correct red, not a deadlock — but the merge protocol must expect it, because the message is neither `is failing.` nor `is expected.`

MERGE PROTOCOL: `scripts/bp-merge.sh`, argument-free, from the PR branch's own worktree. The admin bypass is refused server-side under enforce_admins:true and is no longer this repo's protocol. `allow_auto_merge` stays FALSE on purpose: this fleet stacks branches, and a PR whose checks go green forty minutes later would land into a main that has moved, in an order nobody chose. bp-merge polls and merges in the FOREGROUND.

S2 ADVISORY BY INTENT: the task gate's own harness — it proves the gate CAN fail; requiring it makes the tripwire's tripwire load-bearing
